title: Timeliness of critical value notification from laboratory call logs in a hospital and community network: a retrospective review
abstract: Objective: to measure how often critical values are notified with read-back within 30 minutes of verification and where delays occur. Design: retrospective review of laboratory information system call logs for about 28,000 critical values in 2024 and 2025. Primary outcome: documented read-back within 30 minutes. Results and conclusions will be written after analysis.
introduction: Critical values must reach a responsible clinician quickly, yet compliance with notification standards is rarely measured, and published call-log studies show slower notification for outpatient and community results after hours.
methods: All critical values verified in the period were included. The interval ran from verification to documented read-back, with missing read-back times treated as unsuccessful. Night staffing was linked from rosters. A mixed-effects logistic model with six pre-specified factors examined delay beyond 30 minutes.
results: No data have been analysed yet. The report will present compliance by location and time block, never-notified results, time to read-back and the adjusted model.
discussion: The discussion will compare results with published call-log studies and state where an escalation route or night staffing change would act.
limitations: Documentation rather than clinical action; roster data may miss informal help; no patient outcomes.
conclusion: To be written after analysis; it will describe compliance and its correlates, not the effect of any change.
summary: STROBE and RECORD structured draft with results left empty.
